hypothesis: Who the household is (demographics) and when the snapshot is (calendar) predict 4-week spend.
transformation_description: Baseline: demographic codes, has_demographics, snapshot day index, week-of-year.

hypothesis: A household's recent purchase history predicts its next-4-week spend: lagged 28-day spend windows, trip counts, basket size, recency, tenure, discount usage and spending momentum carry most of the signal.
transformation_description: Added 36 transaction-history features (lagged 28d spend/trips/basket-size windows 1-6, seasonal lag-13, recency, tenure, lifetime spend rate, discount share, evening share, trend ratios) on top of nothing; dropped demographics to isolate signal.
reasoning_summary: Lagged spend correlates 0.82 with the target, far above demographics alone; recent behavior should dominate calendar and demographics.

hypothesis: Channel and basket-mix behavior predicts next-4-week spend: preferred-store share, number of stores used, and department-level spend shares in the last 8 weeks capture where and on what a household spends, beyond raw recency/frequency.
transformation_description: Added 15 features to E001: spend28, trips28, n_stores28, main_store (categorical), main_store_share, and 44 department spend-share columns from the last 56 days.
reasoning_summary: Where a household shops and what it buys (department mix) reflect household size/lifestyle and predict future spend better than recency alone; department shares also proxy for the basket composition that drives totals.

hypothesis: A household's habitual category mix is stable and predicts future spend level beyond recency/level features: department spend shares over 84 days, department diversity, dominant-department share, private-brand orientation, and per-department 28-day spend levels.
transformation_description: Added 24 features to E001 (E002 dropped): 84-day spend shares for 10 largest departments, department diversity count, max department share, private-brand spend share, and 28-day spend in each of the 10 departments.
reasoning_summary: E002 showed store/channel adds nothing, so the unexplored axis is WHAT households buy. High-GROCERY/low-PRODUCE mixes and narrow baskets should mark structurally lower spend; per-department 28d levels give the model category-specific predictors of next-month spend.

hypothesis: Retailer marketing exposure predicts next-4-week spend: number and recency of campaign targeting (TypeA/B/C), campaign-overlap timing, and coupon redemptions add signal about which households will be stimulated to buy in the next 28 days, beyond recent transaction history.
transformation_description: Added 19 marketing features to E001 (E002/E003 dropped): counts of campaigns targeted by type, days since first/last targeting, active/future-campaign overlap flags, redemption counts in 28/84d windows, days since last redemption, redemptions per targeted campaign.
reasoning_summary: Campaign targeting and coupon redemptions are direct retailer actions aimed at specific households; they should shift both the level and timing of next-month spend, information absent from pure purchase-history features.

hypothesis: Richer marketing-exposure signals (full campaign-target/recency set plus coupon-redemption and display/mailer exposure detail) predict next-4-week spend beyond the 19 marketing features already in E004, on top of E001 transaction history.
transformation_description: Evaluated the previously unsaved-but-stored fuller variant of the E004 marketing table (e004_mkt_full.parquet) instead of the trimmed 55-feature version submitted as E004.
reasoning_summary: E004 showed marketing exposure adds little on top of E001 (63.21 vs 63.13), but the fuller table was built and never scored; this tests whether the extra exposure detail (redemptions, display/mailer) changes that conclusion before dropping the family.

hypothesis: Habitual category mix and marketing exposure each add independent signal over transaction history, so combining them should beat both individually (E003: 63.050, E004: 63.212).
transformation_description: Merged E003's 24 category-mix features with E004's 19 marketing features on top of the E001 history base (59+55-2 shared keys = 78 features).
reasoning_summary: E003 and E004 both improved on E001 with disjoint feature families; stacking them should capture complementary household-level information (what they buy vs. what marketing they receive).

hypothesis: The recent-spend→future-spend relationship is multiplicative and compressive (log-log slope ≈0.63): log1p-transformed spend windows plus level-normalized ratios (recent vs trailing average) let the model learn the multiplicative structure and heavy right tail, improving on E003's raw-level features.
transformation_description: Replaced E003's raw-level history features with 20 log1p transforms of spend/trip/product windows (1-4, trailing 12-week, lifetime, long-run rate), EWMA spend, and ratios (recent vs l2/123/long-run), plus capped days-since-last, on top of E003's 24 category-mix features.
reasoning_summary: Spend is heavy-tailed and multiplicative in recent spend (quantile ratio profile, log-log slope 0.63); log transforms and ratios match the data-generating structure so the model can extrapolate the tail instead of being pinned near the mean.

hypothesis: E003's base is saturated at the level of single features; gains come from (a) six screened additions (peak-week spend nwmax12, seasonal lag-12 spend, micro-window spend7, smoothed EWM level, 84d units, recent-spend power transform), (b) separate slope treatment for active vs. recently-inactive households via active/inactive hinges on spend_l123_mean, and (c) a mild positive day-index drift term.
transformation_description: Added to E003: 6 screened history features (nwmax12, nspend_l12, nspend7, nf_pow90_ewm4, nunits84, nf_nspend28_pow90), 4 active/inactive population-split hinges on spend_l123_mean, and day_idx.
reasoning_summary: Offline ridge screening showed these additions and the active/inactive slope split reduce proxy MAE from 63.31 to 62.92 while avoiding coverage-confounded seasonal features; the drift term captures the mild upward spend trend across snapshots.

hypothesis: The 4-week spend signal is concentrated in a few smoothed recent-spend features; a compact, internally-screened 19-feature set beats the saturated 59-70 feature tables (E003/E008) by reducing noise fitting.
transformation_description: Replaced E003's 59 features with 18 features chosen by internal leave-one-snapshot-out forward selection (smoothed recent spend EWMs, recency gaps, zero-week counts, seasonality, one marketing count) plus r_zerow13.
reasoning_summary: Internal LOO ridge screening showed single smoothed-spend features match the full 59-feature set, and the compact subset scored 63.54 vs 64.40 for E003 internally; compactness should reduce overfitting in the official model.

hypothesis: E003's spend_l13 was fake (zero-filled) for 91% of train rows but is real for 94% of validation rows (tenure>=364); replacing fake zeros with NaN, adding has_real_l13 and l13/recent-mean ratio aligns train/val semantics and lets the model use true seasonal-lag signal where it exists.
transformation_description: From E003: spend_l13 set to NaN where tenure<364 (was 0), plus has_real_l13 flag and l13_over_recent ratio (clipped semantics via NaN). All other 59 features unchanged.
reasoning_summary: Validation households are almost all long-tenured, so their lag-13 seasonal spend is real; train rows mostly had a fake zero there, so the model never learned the feature's true meaning. Fixing semantics should let a genuinely predictive seasonal signal transfer to validation.

hypothesis: Demographic segment (age, income level, household size, homeownership, kids) predicts spend level beyond transaction history; the harness never saw history and demographics together.
transformation_description: Added 8 columns to E003's 59: 7 demographic fields (classification_1-5, homeowner_desc, kid_category_desc) + has_demographics flag, merged from the baseline table.
reasoning_summary: Demographics cover ~32% of households and proxy income/size; E001-E010 never combined them with history features, so this signal is untested by the harness model.

hypothesis: E010's l13-NaN fix and E011's demographic segment features are independent improvements over E003; combining them should stack their gains (62.77 or better) since one corrects a leakage-prone feature and the other adds who-the-household-is signal.
transformation_description: Merged E010's table (61 cols incl. has_real_l13, l13_over_recent) with E011's 8 demographic columns; dropped nothing.
reasoning_summary: E010 and E011 each improved on E003 via disjoint column sets; combining them should recover both gains, testing whether the two fixes interact.

hypothesis: Peer-based spend anchors (last-year same-household 4w spend, cohort prior, peer percentiles/ratios) add independent signal over demographics + l13-fix history (E012+E014 union).
transformation_description: E014 (71 cols) + 11 peer-anchor columns from E013's saved table (spend_ly4w, cohort_prior4w, peer_p10/p90, peer_ratio, peer_ratio2, peer_recent28(_med), pop_ratio, anchor_ly_pop, has_ly4w).
reasoning_summary: E013 showed peer anchors are competitive; E012 showed l13-fix + demographics help. If peer anchors are orthogonal to demographics, union should beat 62.713.

hypothesis: Recent-spend signal is best captured by smoothed aggregates (half-life-4/8/13 EWM, 12-week mean/quantiles) plus robust quantiles and micro-structure (stock-ups, basket CV, gaps), which add independent predictive power beyond E012's raw lag windows.
transformation_description: E012 + 57 curated features from saved research tables: EWM half-life 4/8/13 spend, 12-week mean/std/cv/max-share, 28d/14d/7d spend-trips, robust 13-week median/quartiles/max-over-median, zero-week runs, percentiles, basket med/max/cv, stock-up counts, gap stats, unit-price, weekend/morning shares, last-year ratio.
reasoning_summary: E012's top feature correlates 0.822 with the target while unsaved research tables contain smoothed aggregates correlating up to 0.826; adding the strongest of those plus orthogonal micro-structure should lift MAE.

hypothesis: Net discount exposure (loyalty-card, manufacturer-coupon and coupon-match discounts received over the last 84 days, all negative-valued) plus coupon-redemption recency and cyclical week-of-year seasonality add predictive signal over the E014 smoothed base.
transformation_description: E016_smoothed (= full E014 base, 125 feats) + 9 new columns: 84-day sums of retail_disc/coupon_disc/coupon_match_disc (negative-valued), coupon_redemptions_84, days-since-last-coupon, and sin/cos harmonics (period 52 and 26) of snapshot week.
reasoning_summary: Discount dollars proxy for promo-driven stocking and price sensitivity, coupon redemptions proxy for deal-seeking; both plausibly shift next-4-week spend. Weekly per-household population spend varies ~31-39 dollars, so harmonic week terms give the model a cheap seasonal prior.

hypothesis: Trip-timing dynamics predict future spend beyond spend levels: gap rhythm (median/p90 gap, gap EWM, overdue-ness, next-trip ETA, expected trips), zero-28d-window rates over 13/26 windows, active-weeks counts, day-decay EWMs of spend/activity, burst/trend ratios, and snapshot-level macro activity carry independent signal.
transformation_description: E014 base (125 feats) + 33 new household trip-timing/hazard features (overdue_days, overdue_ratio, gap_med/p90/cv_full, gap21_frac, gap_last5 mean/std, gap_ewm5, rhythm_break, next_trip_eta, exp_trips28, n_zero_l13, zero_frac_l13/l26, act_w4/w8/w13, ewm4_d/ewm13_d/ewm_ratio, n_ewm14, burst7, trend14_42, dow_last) + macro per-snapshot columns (m_act7, m_act14, m_spend28_mean/med) + dow_sd.
reasoning_summary: Future spend depends on whether/when the next trips happen, not just how much was spent; gap rhythm, overdue-ness and zero-window rates encode that timing dimension which the spend-level base lacks.

hypothesis: The union of all previously-validated feature families (E016 trip-timing/hazard + smoothed history + demographics + l13-fix + peer anchors + discount exposure + calendar harmonics) is complementary and beats E016 alone on validation MAE.
transformation_description: Merged E016's 157-feature table with E011/E012 demographics + l13-fix columns, E013 peer-anchor columns, and E017-v2 discount/calendar columns (155 features total).
reasoning_summary: Each family added signal in isolation over the same base; E016's timing features were built without demo/peers/discounts, so their union should capture orthogonal components of future spend.

hypothesis: The true union of ALL previously-validated feature families — E016's 31 trip-timing/hazard features (overdue/gap-rhythm/next-trip-ETA/dow/momentum) plus E017's demographics, l13-fix and peer-anchor columns on top of the smoothed history base — outperforms E017's partial union (which accidentally dropped the timing family).
transformation_description: E017's table + the 31 trip-timing/hazard columns from E016's saved table (e018_timing_hazard) that the E017 merge had dropped: overdue_days/overdue_ratio, gap_med/p90/cv/last5, gap_ewm5, rhythm_break, next_trip_eta, exp_trips28, zero_frac_l13/l26, act_w4/8/13, ewm4_d/ewm13_d/ewm_ratio, n_ewm14, burst7, trend14_42, dow_last/dow_sd, m_act7/m_act14, m_spend28_mean/med. Total 184 features.
reasoning_summary: E016 showed timing features add a small gain on the real validation (62.681→62.560); E017's merge silently dropped them, so the intended all-families union was never evaluated. Restoring them completes the union test.

hypothesis: E018's "union" table was incomplete: the retailer-coupon and coupon-match discount features from the validated E017 family were missing (only the merged disc_net_84 was present). Adding the two missing discount-decomposition columns completes the true union of all validated feature families and should slightly improve MAE.
transformation_description: E018's 186-col table + 2 new columns (coupon_disc_84, match_disc_84) from the saved E017 v2 table = 188 features.
reasoning_summary: E015 showed net discount exposure carries independent signal; E018's merge silently dropped the two component columns, so restoring them completes the validated union at negligible noise cost.

hypothesis: E018's table was still incomplete: it lacked the snapshot-day/calendar features (s_day, k_sin/k_cos, r_autocorr, r_dsl, r_gap_mean/ratio, g_mean_l1) from the nf_robust research table. Adding them gives the true union of all validated feature families.
transformation_description: E018's 186-col table + 10 calendar/recency/robustness columns from nf_robust (s_day, k_sin1/k_cos1/k_sin2/k_cos2, r_autocorr, r_dsl, r_gap_mean, r_gap_ratio, g_mean_l1) = 194 features.
reasoning_summary: Every earlier family merge improved MAE; these 10 columns are the last validated-family columns missing from the union, and calendar features are the only way to track the mild upward drift in spend across snapshots.
